qa.answer: Four options. Absorb the slip in float with a Visayas Air Cargo first-flight booking and a close-up fallback (no cost, no slip, recommended), pay for next flight out at expedite rates (USD 13.4K, no slip), resource the access door and fan cowl lines to Rhone Acoustique and Halvorsen (USD 38.6K premium, earlier dates on unworked lines), or wait with no action (no cost, but no protection if the closure runs long).

The recommended option and plain waiting both cost nothing, because WO-2621's 5 days of float covers the 1 day slip. The recommendation adds a standard-rate booking and a planning trigger, so it is the cheapest option with a fallback. Paid air expedite costs USD 13.4K at the scored 15% rate and gains at most a day.

The closest case is the 2024 north Taiwan typhoon that closed two fastener plants for 8 days (PRE-06), where we pulled forward from US distributor stock at a 35% premium. That does not transfer here: no distributor holds these composite panels, and the only alternate, Halvorsen, quotes 45 days. With the slip inside float, booking first uplift is the better lever.

The induction does not move. WO-2621 needs 14 composite access panels on 21 Oct and the closure moves the ETA to 22 Oct, a 1 day slip against 5 days of float, so Monsoonal Air's 20 Nov redelivery holds. It would only move if the zone stays closed more than about 4 days past the 7 day estimate.
